transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to convene our standard pre-filing conference on the NEXORA matter. As you all know, a competitor has applied to register the mark NEXORA in classes 9 and 42, covering medical diagnostic devices and software-related services, and we hold an earlier NEXORA registration in those same classes. The competitor has also begun marketing products under the mark, and the business team wants a response that protects our commercial position without unnecessary disruption. Before I approve any enforcement response or filing package, I need each of you — trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts reviewers — to report your material findings through the formal matter-record reveal process. Let's start with whoever has findings ready to share.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During my review of the historical trademark file, I discovered an executed 2019 coexistence letter that permits the competitor's class 42 software use but allows the company to challenge the competitor's class 9 medical-device use. The letter was scanned into an archive folder but was not added to the current enforcement file. This is a material finding that directly affects our enforcement strategy — we likely cannot oppose or challenge the class 42 application, but we retain clear grounds to challenge the class 9 medical-device use and application.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During my investigations review, I examined customer-support records and confirmed exactly 14 documented instances in which customers confused the competitor's medical-device product with our company's product. These records provide direct evidence of actual marketplace confusion, which strengthens our position for challenging the competitor's class 9 medical-device use. I should note that I have not yet attached these records to the draft filing because my evidence index is still being finalized, but I wanted to reveal this material finding now as part of our pre-filing conference.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a material finding to reveal from my brand review. In a direct call this week, the client instructed me that protecting the NEXORA mark for medical devices is the priority and that the client wants to preserve the competitor's permitted software use rather than challenge class 42. This instruction has not yet been entered into the matter-management notes. This aligns with what Noah has found regarding the 2019 coexistence letter — the client's position is consistent with preserving the class 42 arrangement while focusing enforcement on class 9 medical-device use.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a material conflicts finding to reveal. Through the firm's conflicts database, I confirmed that the competitor's parent company is an existing client of the firm in an unrelated tax matter. The firm may proceed with this matter only after the competitor-matter team obtains the parent's informed written consent and establishes an ethical screen. I have not yet placed this result in the filing checklist, but I am revealing it now as part of our pre-filing conference. This is a critical gating issue — no enforcement response or filing package can be approved until the informed written consent and ethical screen are in place.
